guides.title: Register a sole-proprietor business name
guides.contentMarkdown:
# Register a sole-proprietor business name

A DTI business-name registration gives a sole proprietorship its registered business identity. It is separate from the Business/Mayor’s Permit issued by the municipality where the business operates and from [BIR tax registration](/services/business/tax-registration).

## Who can register

DTI’s BNRS guidance permits a Filipino applicant aged **18 or older** to register a business name. A business using a name other than the owner’s true name must register that name. Foreign nationals and recognized refugees or stateless persons follow DTI’s additional documentary process.

## Prepare the application information

Have the owner’s name, an active email address, business and residence addresses, a proposed business name, and the description of the business activity ready. Choose the territorial scope before submitting. A representative needs a valid ID and an authorization letter signed by the owner, together with the applicable registration requirements.

## Registration steps

1. In the official BNRS **New Registration** service, accept the terms and enter the owner’s information.
2. Select the territorial scope. Enter the proposed dominant business name and choose the business-name descriptor that fits the activity. Use **Check Name Availability**.
3. Save the generated reference code. Complete the business address, owner details, and remaining application fields.
4. Review the information and confirm the undertaking.
5. Pay using a payment channel offered by BNRS. DTI’s guide requires payment within **seven calendar days** of application; an unpaid application is treated as abandoned.
6. After payment confirmation, obtain the certificate. For a later download, use **Transaction Inquiry**, enter the reference code, receive the email verification code, and select the certificate in the downloadable contents.

The official transaction system is **bnrs.dti.gov.ph**. BetterSiquijor provides the guide; DTI receives the application and payment.

## Published registration charges

The following DTI charges appear in the Board of Investments’ **2026 Cost of Doing Business** publication. The total column is the registration fee plus the stated documentary stamp tax.

| Territorial scope | Registration fee | Documentary stamp tax | Calculated total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Barangay | ₱200 | ₱30 | ₱230 |
| City/municipality | ₱500 | ₱30 | ₱530 |
| Regional | ₱1,000 | ₱30 | ₱1,030 |
| National | ₱2,000 | ₱30 | ₱2,030 |

These are DTI business-name charges, not municipal business-permit or BIR transaction charges. Territorial scope concerns where the registered business name may be used for business establishments; DTI says it is not the geographical limit for transacting business. A business-name registration is valid for **five years** from registration.

## After receiving the certificate

Keep the registration certificate and transaction reference. Obtain the Business/Mayor’s Permit from the municipality where the business is located and complete BIR registration. A DTI certificate alone does not authorize business operations.

## Sources and review

- DTI, [BNRS frequently asked questions, live BNRS website](https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/faq): eligibility, name registration, permit distinction, territorial scope, certificate retrieval, and validity.
- DTI, [BNRS registration guide, live BNRS website](https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/resources/registration-guide): application sequence and payment period. The transaction service remains [BNRS](https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/).
- Board of Investments / DTI, [2026 Cost of Doing Business, 11 March 2026](https://boi.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2026-Cost-of-Doing-Business_11March2026.pdf): registration fee and documentary stamp tax schedule.

Source review: **17 November 2026**. The information above is a summary of the issuing agencies’ published instructions.

guides.title: Register a business with the BIR
guides.contentMarkdown:
# Register a business with the BIR

BIR registration records the taxpayer and business for tax administration. It is separate from the DTI business-name certificate and the municipality’s Business/Mayor’s Permit. The BIR identifies three registration routes: the **Online Registration and Update System (ORUS)**, email submission through **NewBizReg**, or the responsible Revenue District Office’s new-business counter.

## Prepare the individual-business documents

The BIR’s business-registration guide lists the following for sole proprietors and professionals:

- Accomplished **BIR Form 1901**.
- Government identification showing the applicant’s name, address, and birthdate; include proof of residence if the ID has no address.
- A valid PRC ID and address-bearing government ID or address proof for a PRC-regulated profession.
- DTI certificate when a business name is used.
- For a representative: a Special Power of Attorney and the representative’s government ID.
- For printing the taxpayer’s own invoices: a clear invoice sample and accomplished **Form 1906**. The guide also provides the alternative of buying BIR Printed Invoices from the RDO.

Corporations and partnerships use **Form 1903** and their applicable SEC registration documents. The correct taxpayer type matters; the individual-business checklist is not a corporate checklist.

## ORUS route

1. Create an ORUS account using the taxpayer’s permanent email address, or sign in to an existing account.
2. Select **New Registration** and the applicable individual or non-individual registration option.
3. Complete the registration details and submit the documents requested for that taxpayer type.
4. Follow the application’s assessment and registration-document instructions.

BIR’s account-setup guide specifies that an existing taxpayer’s ORUS account uses the permanent email already recorded with the BIR. The account is created in the official ORUS system, not on BetterSiquijor.

## NewBizReg email route

1. Scan the applicable documents as PDF files. BIR limits the combined attachments to **4 MB per email**.
2. Complete the tax-type questionnaire and include it with the application documents.
3. Pay the **₱30 loose documentary stamp tax**. An applicant with an existing TIN may use the listed BIR payment channels; an applicant without a TIN follows the RDO’s emailed payment instructions or pays at the new-business counter when collecting the certificate.
4. Select the business location in NewBizReg to identify the responsible RDO, then email the completed application and attachments to that office.
5. Keep the RDO’s acknowledgment. The portal states **three working days from acknowledgment of complete documentary requirements** for manual processing, followed by an email arranging certificate collection and applicable invoice/printing steps.

The published processing period starts with acknowledgment of **complete** documents, not merely sending an email. The RDO’s instructions determine the actual transaction outcome.

## Charges and Siquijor district

The BIR stopped collecting the **₱500 Annual Registration Fee** effective **22 January 2024**, under RMC 14-2024. It should not be added to the NewBizReg steps above. The published **₱30 documentary stamp tax** remains a separate item; invoice printing or purchase is a separate transaction.

Siquijor is included in **Revenue District Office 79 — Negros Oriental and Siquijor**. BIR’s 2026 FOI directory lists the district office at **BIR Building, Agapito Valencia Drive, Barangay Taclobo, Dumaguete City, Negros Oriental**. The same directory publishes **(035) 226-3697** as the RDO’s FOI contact telephone. Use this number for an FOI enquiry; ask the RDO for the registration counter handling your transaction.

## Sources and review

- BIR, [Ways to Register a Business](https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/TP_Guide_on_Business_Registration.pdf): registration channels and documentary requirements.
- BIR, [NewBizReg instructions](https://web-services.bir.gov.ph/newbizreg/): PDF size, questionnaire, documentary stamp tax, acknowledgment, and processing sequence.
- BIR, [RMC 120-2023 attachment — ORUS setup guide](https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RMC%20No.%20120-2023%20Attachment.pdf): account setup and email handling.
- BIR, [RMC 14-2024](https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RMC%20No.%2014-2024.pdf): removal of the Annual Registration Fee.
- BIR, [RMC 117-2026, Annex 2 — FOI receiving officers](https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20No.%20117-2026%20ANNEX%202-compressed.pdf): RDO 79 office address and telephone.

Source review: **17 November 2026**. This page summarizes BIR registration procedures; taxpayer-specific tax classification and obligations are determined by the BIR.

guides.title: Find work through PhilJobNet and PESO
guides.contentMarkdown:
# Find work through PhilJobNet and PESO

**PhilJobNet** is the Department of Labor and Employment’s public job-matching service. Jobseekers can register without a fee, search and save opportunities, see job matches with employer contacts, and respond to invitations from accredited employers.

## Create a jobseeker account

1. Choose **Jobseeker/applicant** on the official PhilJobNet sign-up form.
2. Enter your full name, a valid email address, and a password meeting the form’s requirements.
3. Open the activation email and activate the account. Check the spam folder if it is not in the inbox.
4. Complete the jobseeker profile and job preferences so the system can match relevant opportunities.

The sign-up page requires a password of at least **eight characters**, including a digit, an uppercase character, and a permitted special character. The Bureau of Local Employment’s published client requirements describe jobseekers as Filipino citizens with a Philippine residential address who are **18 or older**. This is the service’s published account-eligibility guidance, not a statement about the legal minimum age for every form of work.

## Search, compare, and apply

- Search or browse job opportunities and save relevant listings.
- Review the employer, work location, qualifications, and application instructions for each vacancy.
- Use the system’s matching results and the employer contact information attached to them.
- Submit an application through the system where supported, or respond to an employer’s invitation using the posting’s instructions.
- Keep the profile and preferences accurate so later matches use the right information.

The platform accredits employers before allowing them to post vacancies. An employer’s accreditation is a platform status; the applicant must still read the individual job’s terms and complete the employer’s selection process.

## Assisted registration through PESO

A jobseeker may also register through the nearest **Public Employment Service Office (PESO)**. The PESO records the jobseeker profile in the **PESO Employment Information System (PEIS)**, which contributes to the National Skills Registry. This is the assisted route for someone who needs help registering or using the online service.

Ask your municipality’s PESO or municipal government about employment-registration assistance. The [local office directory](/government/departments/office-directory) lists municipal office addresses and contacts for all six towns.

## Service cost and account handling

PhilJobNet account creation and its public job-matching services are **free**. BetterSiquijor does not collect job applications, passwords, identity documents, or placement payments. Account activation and job applications are handled by PhilJobNet and the responsible employer or PESO.

## Sources and review

- DOLE Bureau of Local Employment, [About PhilJobNet](https://ble.dole.gov.ph/about-philjobnet/): jobseeker functions, eligibility, and employer accreditation.
- PhilJobNet, [Sign up and account-creation guide](https://philjobnet.gov.ph/signup.aspx): applicant account, email activation, profile completion, and password requirements.
- DOLE PhilJobNet, [Jobs and labour-market information portal](https://philjobnet.gov.ph/): free jobseeker services and accredited employers.
- PEIS, [How to register](https://peis.philjobnet.gov.ph/register.aspx): PhilJobNet registration or assisted registration through PESO.

Source review: **17 November 2026**. These are published service procedures, not a vacancy feed or a promise of placement.
